audit.why: TRICKY / 6/10 sits fine against 49.83% over 576 games — the largest sample in the slice — with Sylas owning 1-5 and Yi taking 6 and 2+ items.
Level 6 as Yi's first claim and first item as the coin-flip match the packet chart, and spikes[1] correctly notes Hijack is low value against a movement ult.
audit.corrected: Sharpened with real cooldowns (Abscond/Abduct 13s to 9s, Kingslayer 12s to 6s) rather than reordered.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chain Lash is written as '(E-into-Q)' and '(E-Q)'; Kingslayer is repeatedly called a shield; and the full layer calls Abscond/Abduct a 'chain-dash stun' in seven places.
audit.why: Chain Lash is Q alone (775 range, 10/9/8/7/6s, damages and slows, then detonates a second time at the intersection). Kingslayer (W) is a lunge that damages and HEALS him — no shield — on 12/10.5/9/7.5/6s, which is why Grievous Wounds decides extended trades (missingInteractions). Abscond is E with an Abduct recast that pulls him to an enemy; Riot's text describes a pull, not a stun, so I wrote pull. Petricite Burst also gives him attack speed and a chain whirl after every cast, which the page never mentioned.
audit.corrected: Chain Lash as (Q); Kingslayer as a heal with anti-heal called for; Abduct as a pull with its real cooldown; Petricite Burst explained.

edits.before: Sylas's Chain Lash poke and shield out-trade your level 1 kit.
edits.after: Sylas's Chain Lash (Q) poke out-trades your level 1 kit hard.

edits.before: At level 2 his E poke and W sustain keep denying your farm.
edits.after: At level 2 his Q poke and Kingslayer (W) heal deny your farm.

edits.before: Sylas dominates levels 1-4: his Chain Lash (E-into-Q) combo pokes hard, and Abscond/Abduct (E) can pull you in for a full rotation while you have no answer. His shield off Kingslayer (W) sustains him through your trades, so farm from range and never step into his E range low.
edits.after: Sylas dominates levels 1-4: Chain Lash (Q) pokes at 775 range on a 10s cooldown and detonates a second time at the intersection, and Abscond (E) recasts into Abduct to pull you back in. Kingslayer (W) heals him off you every 12s, so buy Grievous Wounds and farm from range.

edits.before: First item is skill-dependent: your DPS out-races his mage sustain in a clean duel, but a well-timed Abduct (E) plus Petricite Burst can still burst you before you stick. Bait the E, then commit; that decides the trade.
edits.after: First item is skill-dependent: your DPS out-races his sustain in a clean duel, but Abduct (E) plus Petricite Burst - the attack speed and chain whirl he gets after every cast - can still burst you first. Bait the E on its 9-13s, then commit.

edits.before: Sylas bullies levels 1-4 with his Chain Lash poke, the Abduct (E) pull threat, and a Kingslayer (W) shield-heal that sustains him through anything you throw back. Farm at range, keep your Alpha Strike (Q) for waveclear or an escape, and never sit in his E range while low.
edits.after: Sylas bullies levels 1-4 with Chain Lash (Q) poke, the Abduct (E) pull threat, and a Kingslayer (W) heal that undoes anything you throw back - it falls to a 6s cooldown, so anti-heal matters. Farm at range and keep Alpha Strike (Q) as your escape, not your poke.

edits.before: Land Chain Lash (E-Q) poke and Abduct (E) pull
edits.after: Land Chain Lash (Q) poke into an Abduct (E) pull

edits.before: Shield through your trades with Kingslayer (W) heal
edits.after: Heal through your trades with Kingslayer (W) lunge

edits.before: With E chain-dash online he can stun you out of Alpha Strike's untargetable window the moment it ends, and his Q/W heal undoes your auto poke.
edits.after: With Abscond/Abduct online he pulls you straight back the moment Alpha Strike's untargetable window ends, and Kingslayer's heal undoes your auto poke.

edits.before: Track his E chain-dash (the stun) above all — it is the only thing that reliably catches you after Alpha Strike; bait it or wait it out before you commit. Secondarily count his R, because it steals Highlander.
edits.after: Track Abscond/Abduct (E) above all — 13s at rank 1 down to 9s, and the recast pull is the only thing that reliably catches you after Alpha Strike; bait it or wait it out. Count his R too, though Highlander is a poor steal for him.

edits.before: Hold Alpha Strike to go untargetable through his E chain-dash stun in fights — dodging that one ability is the difference between dying and out-DPSing him.
edits.after: Hold Alpha Strike to go untargetable through the Abduct recast in fights — dodging that one pull, on its 9-13s, is the difference between dying and out-DPSing him.

edits.before: Alpha Strike's untargetable blink dodges his E chain-dash stun and his Q drain damage; his R steals your Highlander, so the ult-vs-ult timing is the lane's core read — never pop yours while his R is up.
edits.after: Alpha Strike's untargetable blink dodges the Abduct pull and Chain Lash's delayed second detonation; Kingslayer heals him off you, so Grievous Wounds decides extended fights; his R can take Highlander, though a movement ult is a weak steal for him.

notes: Kingslayer is a heal, not a shield — the page said 'shield' in four places, which changes the all-in maths and hides the fact that Grievous Wounds is the correct buy here. Chain Lash is Q, not an E-Q combo. I did NOT write 'stun' for Abscond/Abduct anywhere: Riot's text describes a dash with a recast that pulls him to an enemy and says nothing about a stun, so I used 'pull'. If the user knows Abduct applies a brief stun in-game, the remaining full-layer 'chain-dash stun' phrasings in tldr, focus.text and enemyWin can stay; otherwise they need the same treatment. Level chart matches the packet, no chart edits.
